**Visual Analysis of Test Image:**

- **Affected parts**: Whole plant — pseudostems and lower leaves prominently affected
- **Key symptoms observed**:
  - Dark brown/black discoloration on the outer pseudostem leaf sheaths (characteristic streaking/browning)
  - Progressive yellowing and collapse of lower/older leaves
  - Extensive dried, brown leaf bases accumulating at the base
  - The discoloration pattern moves from outer to inner sheaths (classic vascular wilt pattern)
  - New crown growth at the top still appears relatively healthy/green
  - Multiple suckers affected simultaneously

**Reasoning**: The combination of pseudostem sheath browning, progressive outer-leaf collapse, and whole-plant wilt pattern is the hallmark of **Panama Disease** (Fusarium wilt caused by *Fusarium oxysporum* f.sp. *cubense*). This disease causes yellowing of lower leaves progressing upward, brown/dark vascular discoloration in the pseudostem, and eventual plant collapse. The other diseases would show localized leaf lesions (Cordana, Sigatoka, Anthracnose), fruit-end rot (Cigar End Rot), or apical bunching with green streaking (Bunchy Top) — none of which match the whole-plant wilt with pseudostem discoloration seen here.
